The name "Midnight Muse" is not sufficient as a statement of identity on the front panel of a cosmetic product because 21 CFR 701.11(b) requires the statement of identity to be either the common or usual name of the cosmetic, an appropriately descriptive name, a fanciful name understood by the public when the nature of the cosmetic is obvious, or an appropriate illustration or vignette. The provision does not establish that "Midnight Muse" meets any of these criteria, and no source confirms that such a name qualifies as a fanciful name understood by the public [4]. The requirement for the statement of identity to be presented in bold type and in a size reasonably related to the most prominent printed matter on the panel applies, but does not establish acceptance of "Midnight Muse" as an identity [1].

The common or usual name of the cosmetic shall be used as the statement of identity [3].  
An appropriately descriptive name or, when the nature of the cosmetic is obvious, a fanciful name understood by the public to identify such cosmetic may be used [4].  
An appropriate illustration or vignette representing the intended cosmetic use may serve as the statement of identity [5].  

The available regulatory sources do not provide enough information to determine whether "Midnight Muse" qualifies as a fanciful name understood by the public in this context.
